ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under the PCMLTFA and FINTRAC Guidance: all general partners, limited partners, beneficial owners at or above 10%, directors, senior officers and authorized signatories must be screened against Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act, the list of entities subject to Canadian terrorist financing legislation, the OFAC SDN List, and the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List. PEP screening is mandatory for all foreign politically exposed persons, domestic PEPs, and heads of international organizations, with additional negative-news and adverse-media review, ongoing transaction monitoring, and immediate escalation and suspension of formation if any sanctions match or unresolved PEP red flag arises.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec – Services en ligne / Enterprise Name Search and Reservation Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (C.Q.L.R. c. C-11) and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, the enterprise's legal name must be in French. A non-French element is permitted only if it is a recognized registered trademark, a proper name, or accompanied by a French generic or descriptive term. Transliteration or romanization alone is not accepted; a certified French form must be filed for any foreign-language element.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: University, université, college, collège (without professional authorization)
Legal, lawyer, avocat, notary, notaire (unless duly authorized professional body)
Governmental, royal, municipal, police, security (where misleading)
Terms contrary to Quebec public order or moral standards
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the Registraire issues a reasoned refusal notice. The applicant may (i) submit a written reconsideration and request for name modification through the online registry, attaching evidence of distinctiveness and compliance with the Charter of the French Language; (ii) if refused again, file an application for judicial review before the Superior Court of Quebec in accordance with articles 529 et seq. of the Code of Civil Procedure, within 60 days of the refusal; and (iii) in parallel, reserve an alternative compliant name to avoid delaying the limited partnership registration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may be used only as an auxiliary business address; it is not acceptable as the sole registered office for a stevedoring limited partnership. The entity must maintain a genuine physical office in Quebec at which legal process can be served, normally at or near the port terminal, and must hold a valid terminal lease or port authority occupancy agreement. Purely virtual mail-forwarding arrangements do not satisfy Transport Canada, Quebec Port Authority, or Canada Labour Code commercial-substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High – estimated 75% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 12 months, because of Transport Canada marine safety oversight, Quebec port authority audit protocols, Canada Border Services Agency terminal inspections, and occupational health and safety spot checks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c. CCQ-1991), Articles 2236–2260 (société en commandite); An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1), ss. 26–32; Canada Marine Act (S.C. 1998, c. 10), s. 60 for port authority lease
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar), Legal Publicity Service
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) required by s. 26 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital for a limited partnership under the Civil Code of Québec; each limited partner must contribute the agreed cash or property and is liable only up to that contribution (art. 2246 C.c.Q.); contributions in kind must be disclosed in the declaration; no escrow account is mandated by ordinary Quebec law, but any partnership funds deposited for port operations are subject to contractual trust or bond provisions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED that the Board of Directors of [General Partner Inc.], as general partner of [Bulk Port Stevedoring Terminal L.P.], hereby: (1) approves the subscription of the general partner units set out in the unit subscription register and authorizes the execution of the partnership agreement and the filing of the declaration of immatriculation with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; (2) adopts as the registered office the address stated in the declaration, where books and records shall be kept and process may be served; (3) appoints [Name] as Secretary and [Name] as Manager, with authority to open bank accounts, conclude port authority agreements, and execute stevedoring contracts and SWIFT wire instructions on behalf of the Limited Partnership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-formation NUANS name clearance and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Legal Publicity Service, online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an electronic NUANS name search through the REQ platform to verify that the proposed limited partnership name is distinguishable from existing registered names. If available, file a name reservation request (validity up to 90 days) to secure the exact denomination for the intended legal person.
required_dossiers: Proposed limited partnership name (distinctive element plus legal suffix)
NUANS search report
Written authorization from the proposed general partner
Proof of any prior name consent letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to confusing similarity, revise the distinctive element or add an identifiable geographic term and resubmit, or obtain a signed consent from the holder of the conflicting name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the limited partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of Quebec (if an immoveable is contributed) or corporate counsel admitted by the Barreau du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a written partnership agreement satisfying Articles 2236-2260 C.c.Q., identifying the general partner with unlimited liability and each limited partner whose liability is capped to the contributed amount. Set out the contributions, profit-sharing ratio, management powers, dissolution terms, and the statutory object of operating a bulk cargo stevedoring terminal. If real estate or wharf leasehold rights are contributed, execute the contract as a notarial act en minute.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement
Schedule of cash and in-kind contributions with valuations
REQ extracts or birth extracts for all partners
Consents of limited partners and declaration of contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend the agreement by unanimous written consent, then re-execute and notarize any modified page schedule, or if a partner is incapable, withdraw and substitute the partner before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the declaration of immatriculation with the REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online filing service (cre.quebec)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the official declaration d'immatriculation form indicating the LP's name, registered office address in Quebec, object (including NAICS 488320 stevedoring), declared term, total contributions of general partners and of limited partners, and the identity and address of each general partner. Attach the marriage/partnership extract if a natural person. Pay the statutory fee and authorize publication. Retain the acknowledgement number for issuance of the REQ attestation.
required_dossiers: Completed declaration of immatriculation
NUANS report or name reservation certificate
Executed partnership agreement (certified copy)
REQ extracts for corporate general partners
Payment confirmation of the filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon a query for insufficiency, perfect and resubmit the declaration or file a rectifying declaration modificative within the statutory delay (normally 10 days); if the registrar refuses legal form, cure the defect and file a new declaration without losing priority only if the earlier date is maintained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of the governance pack and appointment of officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the General Partner and unanimous resolutions of the limited partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a board meeting of the general partner (or adopt unanimous written resolutions) approving (i) the subscription of partnership units as recorded in the unit subscription register, (ii) the registered office address contained in the declaration, and (iii) the appointments of the Secretary and the Terminal Manager. Circulate the minutes, maintained in the LP's minute book. Confirm the registered office lease or occupancy letter is kept at the place of records.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution
Unit subscription register
Appointment consents of officers
Registered office lease or authorization letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any appointment or subscription is defective, pass a corrective resolution ratified by all partners and keep evidence in the minute book; a defect in consent may be cured by unanimous retroactive ratification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate retrieval, publication check, and opening of banking/payment rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: REQ (attestation) and a Schedule I Canadian bank's commercial treasury unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the publication period, download the official Attestation d'immatriculation from the REQ register and verify the exact legal name, identification number, and partners' disclosure. Open a business banking account in the name of the limited partnership, configure SWIFT wire capabilities and port-authority clearing settlement rails, and complete know-your-client and beneficial ownership attestations required by the AML compliance programme.
required_dossiers: REQ attestation d'immatriculation
Certified copy of partnership agreement
Board resolution appointing bank signatories
AML/KYC questionnaire and beneficial ownership confirmations
Settlement instruction forms for Port Authority Clearing and SWIFT Wire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the partnership documentation, provide certified English/French translations, a certified copy of the resolution, and a fresh REQ attestation; escalate to the treasury compliance committee and, if needed, execute a supplementary signatory resolution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Quebec Port Authority (Administration portuaire de Québec) under s. 60 of the Canada Marine Act; Transport Canada Marine Safety for berth and marine traffic approvals
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Terminal Stevedoring Operating Agreement and Port Access Licence (Licence d'exploitation d'accostage et d'arrimage)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP), Province of Quebec; federal coordination with Environment and Climate Change Canada
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II - Environmental Authorization (s. 22 of the Environment Quality Act, CQLR c. Q-2) for a bulk cargo terminal handling above 250,000 tonnes per year; a full impact assessment under the Impact Assessment Act is required only where federal funding or federal lands are involved or where dredging beyond defined thresholds occurs.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Quebec regulation respecting wastewater discharge and stormwater containment, including total suspended solids limits and post-discharge sampling; fugitive dust must be limited to opacity of less than 20% and sediment controls prevent entry to the Saint-Lawrence River; VOC concentration from equipment and tank vents capped at 120 mg/m³ under applicable provincial air regulations and the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the municipal fire prevention service, structural and crane-load inspections certified by an engineer under the Professional Code (with wharf loading clearance issued by the Port Authority), CNESST occupational health and safety programme for stevedores, WHMIS training, first-aid coverage, and port security clearance under the Marine Transportation Security Regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec; CRA Business Registration Online portal for federal Business Number (BN), GST/HST account and import/export account; Revenu Québec's Registraire des entreprises for the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and QST registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Quebec Limited Partnership formed by foreign entities: (1) file a declaration in the Quebec registre des entreprises to obtain the NEQ; (2) apply to CRA for a Federal Business Number using Form RC1 or Business Registration Online, checking the box for GST/HST and import/export accounts; (3) obtain a CRA business number (BN) incorporating a standard 9-digit business number and a two-letter program suffix; (4) register with Revenu Québec for QST using the same NEQ; (5) complete partnership income tax identification (Partnership Information Return) as required under the Income Tax Act. The LP itself does not receive a separate tax identification number for income tax purposes; partners are allocated taxable income and are separately liable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: A Quebec limited partnership is fiscally transparent for federal and Quebec income tax; income is computed at the partnership level and allocated to partners, who bear tax according to their own status and tax home. For GST/HST and QST, the partnership is a separate registrant when carrying on a taxable supply activity; the general partner is jointly and severally liable for partnership tax obligations unless the partnership is designated as the registrant.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Canada; limited partnerships are inherently pass-through under the Income Tax Act. Partners may allocate income in accordance with the partnership agreement subject to anti-avoidance rules, and may file prescribed designation forms in respect of the partnership using a fiscal year end. For hybrid mismatch arrangements, Canada has enacted hybrid mismatch integrity rules under sections 18.4 to 18.6, 20.5, and associated definitions of the Income Tax Act, which disallow deductible amounts on a structured arrangement where there is hybrid financial instrument duplication or hybrid entity duplication; affected foreign partners may be required to provide information and documentation to the CRA.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) and Quebec Sales Tax (QST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (small supplier threshold; registration becomes mandatory for GST/HST and QST when taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in any single calendar quarter or in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; for non-residents carrying on business in Canada and making taxable supplies, special rules may require registration from the first supply depending on permanent establishment presence and supply characteristics).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No national real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance or digital stamping regime applies to stevedoring or bulk port supplies. Tax invoices must contain prescribed particulars under the Excise Tax Act and the Quebec Tax Administration Act; electronic invoices are acceptable if complete, legible and retained in a processable format. Businesses are required to file GST/HST and QST returns electronically above prescribed thresholds, and must retain records supporting the zero-rating of exported goods for at least six years. Revenu Québec may require certain large registrants to transmit return data electronically through its secure portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of tangible personal property made by a registrant to a non-resident for delivery directly before export from Canada, or to services performed on goods destined for export, including stevedoring and terminal bulk cargo loading, provided the registrant obtains and retains documentary evidence of export within the required time frame. The supply must be made to a non-resident who is the exporter or the freight contract holder, and the goods must be delivered to a carrier or loaded onto an ocean vessel for export. Services such as unloading, weighing, grading and marshalling of bulk cargo at a marine dock for export can qualify as zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act and the analogous QST provisions, provided the services are performed in respect of tangible personal property supplied to a non-resident and not in respect of unexported goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration submitted through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CES) or a border customs export declaration filed with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) where required
Bill of Lading (ocean or rail bill showing consignee and foreign destination)
Commercial invoice or service invoice identifying the stevedoring charges and the exported goods
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent proof of payment and conversion of foreign currency (including SWIFT credit confirmation)
Cargo manifest or port terminal loading report evidencing the transfer of goods to the vessel
Freight contract, booking note or charter party reference linking the non-resident shipper and the export destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess within the normal four-year assessment period, or indefinitely in cases of misrepresentation or fraud. If zero-rating is denied due to insufficient export documentation, the registrant becomes liable for uncollected GST/HST and QST on the full invoice value, plus federal and provincial interest and arrears penalties. Knowingly making a false or deceptive statement or claim under the Excise Tax Act is an offence punishable, upon summary conviction, by fines up to CAD 250,000 and imprisonment for up to two years, and upon indictment, by higher fines and imprisonment up to five years; civil penalties may be assessed of 25% of the tax sought to be evaded or of the net tax understated, and QST penalties analogous in Quebec apply. Repeated failures or fraudulent export zero-rating claims can trigger complete retroactive revocation of the zero-rating, recapture of refunds and denial of input tax credits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), operating jointly with the Department of Finance Canada, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for bank prudential regulation, and FINTRAC for AML compliance under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully floating and freely convertible currency (CAD) with no exchange control statute or administrative FX approval regime. Current account payments (profits, royalties, professional fees, stevedoring service fees) and capital account flows (equity injections, partner capital repatriation, liquidation proceeds) may be executed without Bank of Canada authorization or Minister of Finance license. Constraints arise only from financial crime controls: FINTRAC large-value international EFT reporting at CAD 10,000 and above, OSFI margin and credit rules on the banking counterparty, and the Income Tax Act section 233.1 foreign property reporting obligations of the Quebec Limited Partnership. Profit remittances from Quebec are unrestricted, subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (which may be reduced under the Canada-US Tax Treaty if the recipient is a US resident) and to the Quebec taxation representative appointment rules for a partnership carrying on business in Quebec.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory repatriation timeline, and no forced conversion ratio. The Quebec bulk-port stevedoring entity may retain proceeds in any foreign currency (USD, EUR) in a foreign currency-denominated account at a Schedule I bank or an authorized foreign bank branch in Canada. Compliance obligations are limited to accurate record-keeping under the Income Tax Act, FINTRAC EFT reporting thresholds, and the OECD Balance of Payments statistical reporting administered by Statistics Canada. No Bank of Canada approval is required to fund offshore operating accounts or to pre-settle trade liabilities at Foreign Exchange.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border electronic money institutions (EMIs) and foreign payment service providers are rated Low-to-Medium on the treasury viability scale for this Quebec stevedoring mandate. Unlicensed non-resident EMIs cannot serve as primary settlement or escrow rails because Canada has enacted the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), under which payment service providers must be registered directly with the Bank of Canada; the registration transition window began September 2024 and existing providers must hold an RPAA registration or transitional status to operate into September 2025. The Quebec LP may lawfully use a registered RPAA intermediary for small-value disbursements (crew payments, per-diem allowances) but the Capital Escrow Account and the port-authority clearing relationship must reside with a prudentially regulated Schedule I bank or a licensed Quebec credit union. Legal constraints: foreign EMIs are not authorized to accept deposits under the Bank Act, their balances are not CDIC-insured, and the Export Development Canada trade settlement programs do not accept EMI counterparties.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For de novo onboarding of a non-resident Quebec Limited Partnership, Canadian Schedule I banks generally require an in-branch, in-person KYC and account-activation interview with at least one general partner and one mandated signatory who holds Canadian presence or can travel to Quebec; remote video onboarding is available only within established relationship banking frameworks or via RPAA-registered digital banks, and such remote-only approvals carry lower transaction limits and stricter monitoring. Documentary execution by foreign directors requires notarized signature guarantees, apostilled or legalized corporate extracts from the partnership registrar (Registraire des entreprises du Quebec), and a certified copy of the deed of partnership. The banks typically require a Montreal-area registered address, a Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), and, where the LP will carry on business in Quebec, the appointment of the general partner as the representative with tax residency filings. If no principal can appear physically, a medium-tier onboarding outcome is realistic with enhanced conditions, an OSFI-compliant CDD file, and a 90-day funding moratorium pending compliance review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner opacity typical of Limited Partnership capital structures, including limited partners holding participation above 25% or outside Canada.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete capital account register with NEQ extract; deed of partnership executed by the general partner; UBO declaration mapping all individuals or legal entities ultimately owning or controlling 25% or more of the partnership; attestation of economic substance (Quebec business address, employment records, local port operating licenses); and consent forms authorizing CDD verification under PCMLTFA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds inquiry on the initial capital escrow injection wired from an offshore jurisdiction or corporate hub.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription and contribution agreements; 12-month bank statements of each contributor; employer or commercial accounts receivable records proving unrelated sourced income; foreign country corporate extracts where contributing entities are domiciled; and a SWIFT gpi trail with explicit originator and beneficiary references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity international EFT activity from trade disbursements to charterers, vessel agents, and port authorities triggering FINTRAC EFT and large-value monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current terminal handling agreements and stevedoring service contracts; port authority tariff schedules and invoice ledger; International Maritime Organization vessel registration extracts; Quebec gas/oil and marine supplier invoices; payroll registers for the stevedore workforce; and a treasury policy demonstrating no third-party payment pushes without underlying contractual support.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Red flags arising from payments to politically exposed or sanctioned jurisdictions, or to port agents using nominee account structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial registry extracts and UBO declarations of each charterer and port agent; comprehensive OFAC, Canada Criminal Code, and UN sanctions screening results; bank guarantee, standby LC, or cash collateral cover on high-value invoices; Quebec supplier registration proof (Liste de fournisseurs with GST/QST numbers); and a signed PCMLTFA-compliant attestation that no nominee accounts or shell intermediaries are used for settlement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for inbound capital injections to the Quebec LP capital escrow and operating accounts follows SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 where interbank positioning is required) from the subscribing partner's bank to the Schedule I receiving institution in Montreal or Quebec City, with receipt credited through Payments Canada Lynx or ACSS. The instruction must reference the partnership bank account IBAN-equivalent number, SWIFT BIC of the receiving branch, CAD or USD settlement currency, and an information line containing the NEQ registration, the subscription agreement number, and the UBO declaration. Canada does not employ a uniform outward cross-border purpose code system comparable to the China BOP scheme; however, the receiving bank maps the narrative to an internal purpose reason code and must apply FINTRAC EFT record-keeping rules for international transfers of CAD 3,000 or more, and EFT reporting for CAD 10,000 or more. The bank will require pre-funding clearance letters, an executed escrow agreement for initial shareholder capital, and confirmation that the funds are free from prescribed drug or criminal proceeds before credit enhancement or interest accrual.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound stevedoring trade settlement rails comprise: (1) SWIFT MT103 direct customer wires for charterer remittances, international agent fees, and foreign supplier invoices; (2) SWIFT MT202COV two-sided bank positioning for substantial disbursements; (3) commercial documentary letters of credit governed by UCP 600 and eUCP for bulk-handling equipment, marine bunker purchasing, and terminal capex; (4) domestic CAD clearing via Payments Canada ACSS and Lynx for compliant disbursements of payroll for stevedores, dock supervisors, equipment mechanics, and wharfage charges to the port authority; and (5) multi-currency netting through an OSFI-regulated custody account where the LP maintains operational USD and CAD ledgers. Where the counterparty is a Quebec port terminal operator, Port_Authority_Clearing designations apply, requiring bank confirmation of port concession agreements and tenant licence credentials before releasing funds to the dock operator. All disbursements are subject to a six-eye review, independent OFAC and Criminal Code sanctions screening, and the corporate treasury mandate prohibiting bearer instruments or uncollateralized telegraphic transfers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla deliverable foreign exchange forwards quoted by Schedule I bank dealing rooms for CAD/USD and CAD/EUR, tenors up to 24 months, collateralized under ISDA and CSA credit support documentation.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing offshore currencies commonly used by international charterers and vessel operators (BRL, NGN, INR, ARS) where CAD is the settlement leg and the NDF satisfies the Quebec LP operational invoice exposure.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps between CAD floating-rate (CDOR/SOFR equivalent) and USD or EUR fixed-rate legs, used for long-dated terminal infrastructure financing and stevedoring equipment leases.
European-style foreign exchange options and zero-cost collars transacted under a confirmable ISDA 2002 Master Agreement for protection against adverse CAD appreciation on US-dollar revenue receipts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (Quebec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: no later than the 15th day of the month following the annual registration anniversary of the LP; if REQ issues a reminder notice, the date on the notice is controlling (commonly June 15 for calendar-year registrations).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late notice from REQ; continued default triggers administrative deregistration (radiation) of the LP and publication in the Gazette officielle; general partner may lose the benefit of registration and face personal liability toward third parties for obligations contracted during the default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Canadian Partnership Information Return (T5013 Summary and T5013 slips)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the end of the partnership fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year fiscal period, the return is due May 31 of the following year and T5013 slips must be provided to partners by March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty of $25 per partner per month (minimum $100, maximum $2,500 per partnership); separate penalties of $50 per missing T5013 slip; a partnership that knowingly fails to file may be subject to an additional 5% penalty on unreported amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Relevé 15 – Annual Partnership Information Return (Revenu Québec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year partnership, the Relevé 15 must be filed and distributed to partners no later than March 31 of the following year; for non-calendar fiscal periods, within the same deadline period as the federal T5013.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 1% of the amounts to be reported, plus 1% per month of delay up to 3%; knowingly filing false or incomplete returns may incur criminal fines and penal provisions under the Taxation Act (Quebec).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is triggered by revenue thresholds for a Quebec Limited Partnership. An audit becomes compulsory when required by the partnership agreement, a private debt covenant, or a federal port authority terminal operating agreement; otherwise a review engagement under Canadian standard for review engagements is generally sufficient.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Partnership financial statements are prepared in accordance with Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under the CPA Canada Handbook; IFRS is adopted only where the partnership or a consolidating general partner is a publicly accountable enterprise.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The REQ annual declaration is used to confirm current general partners and any partner holding at least 25% of the LP. Any change in beneficial ownership or partner status must be filed with REQ within 15 days of the change. The LP must also circulate a written UBO confirmation to all limited partners once per year and update the internal ownership register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited and General Partners
Register of Acquisitions, Transfers and Redemptions of Partnership Interests
Minute Book containing partnership resolutions, amendments and equity decisions
Register of Registered Office and Preferred Postal Addresses

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal 15% + Quebec 11.5% = 26.5% combined general corporate rate; LP is fiscally transparent, no entity-level tax, income taxed at partner level
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED (federal 15% non-refundable / 35% refundable for CCPC; Quebec 14% refundable / 30% non-refundable); accelerated CCA on eligible port equipment; Quebec refundable on-the-job training credit; LP pass-through eliminates entity-level corporate income tax

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Summary + T5013-MTA (Partnership Information Return) filed via CRA EFT (Electronic Filing for Returns) / My Business Account
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 5 months after the LP fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end due May 31 of the following year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, CRA business number (BN), mailing address, and fiscal period of the limited partnership
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide a complete schedule of non-resident partners; use a verifiable Canadian registered office address

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting year-end date in YYYY-MM-DD format
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match the LP agreement; absence of a fixed period may result in CRA imputing a calendar year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NAICS 488320 / ISIC 5224 for marine bulk cargo stevedoring terminal operations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact NAICS code to avoid misclassification and TP audit flags

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total stevedoring revenues, operating costs, dock charges, and terminal handling expenses at the LP level
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose intercompany throughput fees and any non-arm's length transactions separately

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of net income or loss to each partner per the LP agreement and ITA s. 96
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate only Canadian-source business income to non-resident partners; attach T5013-MTA Schedule 13

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each partner's name, address, residency status, ownership percentage, and share of income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify country of residence and treaty position; attach certificates of residence where reduced withholding is claimed

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: ITA s. 162(7): C$25 per day late, minimum C$100, maximum C$2,500; for partnerships with more than 50 partners, maximum C$2,500 per day; false or omitted information: C$100 per partner under s. 162(7.3); late T106: C$100 per day up to C$24,000 (s. 162(7.1))

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Relevé 13 (Quebec Partnership Information Return) filed via Revenu Québec Télétransmission (EDT)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 5 months after the LP fiscal year-end under the Quebec Tax Administration Act (LAF), s. 36

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), GST/QST accounts, LP legal name, and registered address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must be disclosed; furnish the Quebec address of the partnership's principal establishment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B - Fiscal period and income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual income, expenses, and net income for Quebec tax purposes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Quebec-source income must be segregated from foreign-source income for non-resident allocation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of Quebec taxable income to each partner in accordance with the LP agreement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must report their Quebec share via Relevé 15; treaty reductions require a TRC on file

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Québec late filing: C$25 per day, minimum C$100, maximum C$2,500 (TA Act s. 34.2); misstatement: 5% of the unreported amount plus 1% monthly interest; gross negligence: 50% penalty

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII (ITA s. 212(2)) on payments characterized as dividends; LP profit allocations are not Part XIII dividends — non-resident partners are taxed under Part I on their share of Canadian-source business income (up to 53.31% top marginal rate for Quebec individuals; 26.5% combined for corporate partners); guaranteed interest or management fees paid to non-resident partners are subject to 25% Part XIII
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident partner must: (1) obtain a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the home tax authority; (2) file Form NR301 (Quebec) or NR302 with CRA to invoke treaty benefits; (3) deliver the TRC and approved form to the LP before the payment date; (4) for Part I relief on business profits, file Form T1 or T2 and rely on the DTA business-profits article absent a fixed base/PE; (5) retain all documentation for six years for CRA audit

stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory (s. 212(1)(d)); treaty-reduced to 10% under the Canada-US and Canada-UK DTAs (subject to Form NR301 + TRC). Interest: 25% statutory (s. 212(1)(b)); reduced to 0% on arm's length interest under the Canada-US protocol and 0% under the Canada-UK DTA. The LP must withhold Part XIII on any guaranteed interest, rent, or royalty payments to non-resident partners; failure triggers director liability.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: C$1,000,000 aggregate reportable transactions with non-arm's length non-residents (T106 filing threshold); Master File required where consolidated group revenue is at or above C$500,000,000 and cross-border reportable transactions exceed C$5,000,000; documentation must be produced within 6 months of a CRA request under s. 247(4)
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not impose Caribbean-style ESR, but s. 245 ITA GAAR and sham doctrine void transactions lacking commercial substance; a stevedoring LP must demonstrate real presence through terminal assets, dock cranes, licensed labour, port authority contracts, invoicing, and Quebec bank accounts to preserve pass-through integrity

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully evading federal or Quebec tax through false declarations, inflated expenses, unreported stevedoring revenue, or forged T5013/Relevé 13 filings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax (s. 163(2) ITA); criminal conviction under s. 239(1) ITA: fine from 50% to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years; Quebec parallel penalties under the Tax Administration Act
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for restitution; criminal convictions may impose travel bans, seizure of terminal assets, revocation of port licences, and imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misuse of the LP pass-through structure: synthetic allocations, artificial losses, treaty-shopping through a zero-tax jurisdiction, or circular financing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA reassessment denying the tax benefit; s. 245(7) GAAR penalty of 25% of the denied benefit (effective for transactions after April 2023); Quebec GAAR under s. 1075.2.1 of the Taxation Act
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Civil Code of Quebec art. 317 the corporate veil is pierced where the LP is a sham; directors personally liable for the full reassessed tax, interest, and penalties

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Stevedoring services, throughput fees, management charges, or equipment leases priced outside arm's length with a related foreign shareholder; T106 omitted or misstated
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: s. 247(2) TP adjustment; s. 247(3) penalty of 10% of the adjustment where it exceeds C$5,000,000 or 10% of gross revenue; late T106 filing penalty of C$100 per day up to C$24,000
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in false TP documentation face criminal prosecution under s. 239; CRA may apply s. 227.1 to impose director liability for unremitted amounts flowing from the adjustment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold 25% (or treaty-reduced) Part XIII tax on non-resident partner allocations, deemed dividends, guaranteed interest, royalty, or management fee payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: s. 227(8) ITA: 10% late-withholding penalty plus daily interest; s. 227.1: directors jointly and severally liable for up to 15% of the unremitted amount; Revenu Québec imposes the same regime
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable, without proof of intent, for unremitted Part XIII and interest; Quebec LAF provides parallel director liability and may bar directors from leaving the province pending settlement

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the LP without real port-terminal substance, concealing beneficial ownership, or lacking basic AML controls over high-volume port clearing and Swift/Wire payment flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PCMLTFA administrative monetary penalty up to C$2,000,000 per violation; suspension of the port operator licence; CRA sham-entity reassessment with full tax restitution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors liable under PCMLTFA s. 74(1) for fines up to C$500,000 (individuals) and imprisonment up to 5 years; travel prohibitions and extradition exposure under Canada's Mutual Legal Assistance arrangements
